articleTitle: The real-time implementation of emitter identification for ESM
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing in Electronic Warfare
abstract: It is shown that no computer architecture is available providing a very high Prolog execution capability within a real-time environment. The experience gained, however, has permitted the architecture of a suitable parallel computer to be specified. The PSIDRA architecture is based on a Sequential Prolog Processor capable of 5 MLIP operation. Two Sequential Prolog processors are integrated with a Scheduler Processor to form the basic Prolog Processing Node. The PSIDRA Computer integrates these Nodes within a real-time multi-sequential operating environment. The architecture is both highly scalable and designed to meet the stringent requirements of real-time operation of programs such as CEIM and PALANTIR.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing in Electronic Warfare
abstract: As well as being able to implement more effectively conventional ECM techniques such as false targets and noise jamming, the digital radio frequency memory offers the capability to generate a wider variety of jamming waveforms. This paper discusses some ideas for jamming based on digital modulation techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Antenna beamforming for EW using adaptive layered networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing in Electronic Warfare
abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANNs) provide an alternative 'inverse processing' solution for angle-of-arrival (AOA) estimation in the form of an adaptive layered network. A suitably trained supervised ANN, such as the multi-layer perceptron, can classify signal AOA into a number of sectors with processing input taken directly from the receiving array elements. The main problems are that uniform angular sectoring is not compatible with linear array functions, and unless the output space is carefully code-mapped, rays with AOA near the boundaries will give large estimation errors. These and other problems were resolved by modifying the ANN method using least squares and a novel graphical solution together with unit distance (Gray) coding.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generic techniques for the identification of wanted and unwanted modulations on pulses
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing in Electronic Warfare
abstract: The author looks at pulse modulation from the point of view of the laws of physics, the radar designer, the measuring device and the analysis system, and defines some important properties before putting these ideas together and suggesting some of the features that will be required from a modulation parameter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing in Electronic Warfare
abstract: The analysis of signals received in an ESM system increasingly requires some form of pre-detection processing to aid in the sorting of signals, in discrimination of small signals proximate to powerful emitters, in the detection and processing of low energy signals, and for additional characterisation. It is desirable to achieve such processing in the most efficient and cost-effective manner, and there are three competing technologies which can be applied, RF, optical and digital. This paper presents an overview of the potential performance offered by the digital option in the context of a frequency channeliser for an ESM receiver.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A procedure for clock alignment of widely dispersed mobiles in frequency hopped communications scenario
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing in Electronic Warfare
abstract: A novel clock alignment procedure for randomly dispersed mobiles is described and numerically modelled using discrete-event simulation, incorporating procedures for time-stamping and sub-netting. The model establishes a common local time within sub-nets under sub-net management control, which allows for both late net entries and early leavers. An example is presented using a number of mobiles dispersed over a wide geographical area, which have both random clock drift and random initial time offsets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spread-spectrum PN-coded waveform detection for communications ESM
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing in Electronic Warfare
abstract: The feedback function of the linear feedback shift register, which generates the coded sequences employed in spread-spectrum systems for the spreading function, is detected by the use of triple correlation analysis. This allows the pseudonoise (PN) code to be determined for correct waveform demodulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
